papers.what_it_is: A short theory paper that defines a multi-valued quantum neuron with roots-of-unity inputs, weights and outputs, maps energy levels to those roots, and works a max/min example by hand; no experiment or numerical training run.

existing.note: The claim is stated in the abstract only. The body supports no comparison: the high-functionality statement is attributed to cited work on complex-valued networks, and the paper reports no convergence experiment.

existing.reader_inference: The paper contains no training run, no convergence measurement and no comparison with a binary-input quantum neural network. The nearest support is the citation in Section IV about complex-valued networks versus real-valued ones, which is not a quantum-versus-binary comparison.

existing.reader_inference: Equation (1) is cost = k times r times d with d = log N / log r. The step from radix 3 to |0>, |1> and one superposition state is the author's reading.

papers.title_in_file: SCOOP: A Quantum-Computing Framework for Constrained Combinatorial Optimization (arXiv:2504.10897v2)
papers.version_note: The text layer carries the paper twice (two extraction passes); both agree. Figures 2 to 4 are plots: the pages were also viewed as images, and plotted values are used only in reader_inference, read by eye.
papers.what_it_is: A framework paper (SCOOP) that turns constrained combinatorial problems into unconstrained profit problems for QAOA with classical post-processing, with three theorems on twin problems and PennyLane simulations on 3-regular graphs of 6, 8 and 10 nodes.

existing.note: The paper gives the statement and its conditions: the theorem is attributed to reference 36, applies to simple undirected graphs without isolated vertices, and is proved only as a sketch. The stored value gave sentences about the theorem, not its statement.
existing.value: The paper states as Theorem 1, attributed to reference 36, that for any graph G a dominating set of size k exists if and only if G has a vertex subset PD with profit pPD = |V | − k; the section covers simple undirected graphs without isolated vertices; the proof is given as a sketch.
quotes: Theorem 1. [36] For any graph G = (V, E), G has a dominating set DS
⊆ V of size k if and only if G has a subset PD ⊆ V with profit pPD = |V | − k.
In this section, we refer to simple undirected graphs without isolated vertices.
Proof. (Sketch)
existing.certainty_reason: Section IV states the theorem with its conditions; the proof is a sketch and the theorem is credited to reference 36.
existing.reader_inference: In the sketch of the forward direction the paper writes pPD = |E| − k, where the theorem says |V | − k; this reads as a typo for |V |. The sentence 'Theorem 1 below concludes the proof that MINDS and MAXPD are SCOOP twins' also uses the theorem as the last step of the twin proof.

existing.note: The 60% figure is a summed probability over the best solutions (the paper counts the second and third best as near-optimal), averaged over 10 random graphs; it is not the probability of the single best solution, which the paper puts lower.

(we include the second and third best solutions)

existing.reader_inference: Read by eye from Figure 3, the over-60% value holds for the SCOOP profit-domination curve. The penalty-based dominating-set curve in the third column is lower at p = 1 for n = 10 (about 0.3 against about 0.9).

quotes: Our framework guides the derivation of an unconstrained COP from the constrained COP. This process results in a penalty-free cost Hamiltonian that is well-suited for QAOA.
Subsequently, the viable solutions obtained by QAOA are efficiently post-processed.

assertions.value: The paper defines SCOOP twins by four conditions on a constrained and an unconstrained problem: identical input domains, solution containment, objective function compatibility through a polynomial-time computable function, and solution enhance-ability by polynomial-time post-processing.

quotes: Identical Input Domains: The problems share the same input domain I, i.e., I = IC = IU .
Solution Containment: for every instance x ∈ I, SolC (x) ⊆ SolU (x).
Objective Function Compatibility: For any x ∈ I there exists a polynomial-time computable function fx
Solution Enhance-ability: For each x ∈ I, and each s ∈ SolU

assertions.value: The paper gives a five-step process to derive an unconstrained twin from a constrained problem: identify the constraints, quantify how far an infeasible solution satisfies them, build the objective, prove objective function compatibility, and prove solution enhance-ability.

Step 4 Prove

papers.title_in_file: Effect of barren plateaus on gradient-free optimization (arXiv:2011.12245v2; published in Quantum 2021)
papers.version_note: The text layer carries the paper twice (two extraction passes); both agree. Figure 3 was not viewed as an image; its plotted values are not used.
papers.what_it_is: A theory-plus-simulation paper that proves cost-function differences are exponentially suppressed in a barren plateau (Proposition 1, Corollary 1) and shows by simulation that shot counts for Nelder-Mead, Powell and COBYLA grow exponentially with qubit number on a variational compiling task.

existing.note: The result is a statement about the variance of the cost difference, with the mean zero, under stated conditions: the cost has the form of Eq. 1, it exhibits a barren plateau by Definition 1, and the number of parameters and the distance between the points are polynomial in the number of qubits. The proof gives an upper bound on the second moment.
existing.value: The paper proves in Proposition 1 that, if the cost exhibits a barren plateau according to Definition 1, the expected difference of the cost between two points is zero and its variance is exponentially vanishing with the number of qubits, under the assumptions that the number m of parameters is polynomial in the number of qubits and that each parameter sets a unitary generated by an operator with two distinct non-zero eigenvalues.
quotes: The following proposition constitutes the main result of our work. The proof is presented in the Appendix.
If the cost exhibits a barren plateau according to Definition 1, then the expectation value of the difference
and the variance is exponentially vanishing with n as
we assume that the number m of parameters in θ is in O(poly(n)).
This proposition asserts that the variance of cost function differences is exponentially suppressed in a barren plateau.
existing.certainty_reason: Proposition 1 is stated in Section 3.1 with its conditions and proved in Appendix A.
existing.reader_inference: The Appendix bounds the second moment from above (a Cauchy-Schwartz bound giving m squared times L squared times F(n)). This is an upper bound on how large typical differences are; it does not say that every pair of points has a small difference.

existing.note: The Discussion also states that careful choice of optimization strategy may extend the size limits of trainable problems, and that the exponential scaling is asymptotic; see the new assertions.
quotes: Our work casts doubt on the notion that the choice of optimizer could provide a strategy to avoid barren plateaus.
Proposition 1 is relevant to gradient-free optimizers that search through the landscape starting from a (random) initial point.
existing.certainty_reason: Section 5 states the scope of the result.

papers.what_it_is: A short letter with three exact identities (Fourier expansion of a quantum kernel as an entangling tensor kernel contraction, feature-wise grouping, and kernel target alignment as a Fourier-coefficient cosine similarity) and a numerical test of MPO compressibility on random layered feature maps with two and three features.

assertions.value: The authors state that, in the spectral tensor network, the bond dimension measures the correlations required to represent the kernel's Fourier modes, that this notion differs from the entanglement-based bond dimension of quantum states, and that a low-rank spectral structure can exist even when the feature map acts on an exponentially large Hilbert space.
quotes: This notion of bond dimension differs from the usual tensor network description of quantum states
can exhibit a low-rank spectral
structure even when the feature map acts on an exponentially large Hilbert space.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' interpretation of their identity.

assertions.value: The authors state that the singular values of the matricization across a cut are the operator Schmidt coefficients, that the minimum exact MPO bond dimension is the number of their nonzero entries (the operator Schmidt rank), and that truncating to a smaller bond dimension gives an approximation whose error is controlled by the discarded Schmidt weight.
quotes: the minimum exact MPO bond dimension is their number of nonzero entries, i.e. the operator Schmidt rank.
Truncating to a smaller
bond dimension retains only the leading Schmidt coefficients and gives a low-bond-dimension approximation of the quantum kernel whose error is controlled by the discarded Schmidt weight.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated without proof in the paper; it is a standard tensor-network fact the paper does not derive.

For d = 2 and d = 3 these are small.

assertions.value: The authors state that a feature map generating a large Hilbert space does not by itself imply a hard kernel, that kernels with rapidly decaying operator Schmidt spectra can be evaluated classically with small bond dimension and are unlikely to give an advantage based on kernel evaluation alone, and that slowly decaying spectra identify stronger candidates for quantum advantage.
quotes: but this does not by itself imply a hard kernel.
the kernel admits a compact spectral
tensor network representation and can be evaluated classically with small bond dimension.
Such kernels are therefore unlikely to provide an advantage that relies on the complexity of kernel evaluation alone.
are stronger candidates for quantum advantage based on kernel evaluation.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own interpretation, not tested for any real dataset.
assertions.reader_inference: The optimization in the paper uses the target kernel's exact coefficient tensor, which for many features is exponentially large. The paper does not show that the small-bond-dimension MPO can be obtained without that tensor, so it is not shown that the kernel can be evaluated classically by this route.

assertions.value: The authors state that the compressibility of the Fourier coefficient tensor should be treated as a central diagnostic for quantum kernels, and that classical representability is governed by correlations in frequency space rather than only by circuit depth, Hilbert space dimension or entanglement in the feature state.
